en.title: Protecting intellectual property in ASEAN: trade marks and mediation
en.standfirst: How to protect trade marks and other intellectual property in ASEAN markets: the first-to-file risk, filing country by country, and WIPO-ASEAN mediation.
en.metaDescription: Protect your intellectual property in ASEAN: first-to-file risk, filing trade marks country by country, and WIPO-ASEAN mediation for disputes.
en.body:
Businesses planning to sell or manufacture in ASEAN should put **intellectual property protection** in place before launching in each target market.

Trade mark, patent and design rights are territorial. For companies preparing to **register IP in Indonesia, Singapore or other ASEAN markets**, early searches and a deliberate filing strategy help address risks such as **trade mark squatting**. Where a dispute arises, **WIPO-ASEAN mediation** may assist with eligible matters.

## The first-to-file risk

Trade mark squatting involves another party seeking registration of a brand before its intended owner establishes protection in the market.

Early filing matters in jurisdictions using a first-to-file approach. Indonesia is among the ASEAN countries where trade mark rights are generally granted on that basis.

Do not assume that earlier use elsewhere automatically determines the outcome of a local dispute.

Search the target market's trade mark records before launch and obtain advice where an existing application or registration may affect your plans.

## No single ASEAN IP right

There is no single ASEAN-wide trade mark or patent registration covering the whole region.

Plan protection by jurisdiction and by type of right. The markets where you sell and the locations where you manufacture may both be relevant to that assessment.

A registration in your home jurisdiction does not automatically become a registration in an ASEAN jurisdiction. The position differs by type of IP and claim, so assess the rights relevant to your business.

Identify the rights requiring local protection and the available application routes before filing.

## Filing routes: the Madrid System and national applications

The Madrid System, administered by WIPO, allows eligible applicants to seek trade mark protection in multiple participating jurisdictions through one international application based on a home application or registration. Each designated jurisdiction still decides whether protection is granted under its own laws.

Taiwan is not a member of the Madrid System. Applicants based in Taiwan therefore cannot use a Taiwanese application as the basis for an international Madrid filing. In practice, trade marks for ASEAN markets must be filed country by country with the national IP office of each market, or through a local agent or attorney in each jurisdiction.

Madrid does not create a global trade mark and does not register patents. Direct national applications are the standard route for many applicants and may be appropriate even for those who are eligible to use Madrid.

Choose the route around the brand, the goods or services and the jurisdictions involved.

## WIPO-ASEAN mediation

Where a dispute arises, the WIPO-ASEAN Mediation Programme (AMP+) provides a mediation framework for eligible IP and technology matters.

The programme offers funding support subject to its conditions. Confirm current eligibility and availability with WIPO. [WIPO: ASEAN Mediation Programme](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/office-singapore/wipo-asean-mediation-programme)

Mediation requires agreement to participate and does not guarantee settlement. It should be considered alongside the circumstances of the dispute and the enforcement options available in the relevant jurisdiction.

The agency identified in this guide is WIPO, for Madrid administration and its mediation services. Local registration is handled by the national IP office in each ASEAN market.

zh.title: 在東協保護智慧財產權：商標與調解
zh.standfirst: 如何在東協市場保護商標及其他智慧財產權：先申請先取得的風險、逐國申請，以及 WIPO 與東協的調解機制。
zh.metaDescription: 在東協保護您的智慧財產權：先申請先取得的風險、逐國申請商標，以及透過 WIPO 與東協調解計畫處理爭議。
zh.body:
計劃在東協銷售或生產的企業，應在進入每一個目標市場之前，先完成**智慧財產權保護**的布局。

商標、專利與設計權利均具有地域性。對於準備**在印尼、新加坡或其他東協市場登記智慧財產權**的公司而言，及早檢索並制定明確的申請策略，有助於因應**商標搶註**等風險。若發生爭議，**WIPO 與東協的調解機制**可協助處理符合條件的案件。

## 先申請先取得的風險

商標搶註是指第三方在品牌真正所有人於當地取得保護之前，先行申請該品牌的商標登記。

在採行先申請先取得制度的司法管轄區，及早申請十分重要。印尼即屬於商標權利通常依此原則授予的東協國家之一。

切勿假設在其他地區較早使用，就能自動決定當地爭議的結果。

進入市場前，應先檢索目標市場的商標登記資料；若既有的申請案或登記案可能影響您的計畫，請尋求專業意見。

## 沒有單一的東協智慧財產權

目前並不存在涵蓋整個區域的單一東協商標或專利登記制度。

請按司法管轄區及權利類型分別規劃保護。您銷售產品的市場與生產所在地，都可能需要納入評估。

在您母國取得的登記，不會自動成為東協任一司法管轄區的登記。各類智慧財產權與權利主張的情況不同，請就與您業務相關的權利逐一評估。

申請前，先確認哪些權利需要在當地取得保護，以及可採用的申請途徑。

## 申請途徑：馬德里體系與各國國內申請

由 WIPO（世界智慧財產權組織）管理的馬德里體系，讓符合資格的申請人得以基於母國的申請案或登記案，透過一件國際申請，在多個參與的司法管轄區尋求商標保護。各被指定的司法管轄區仍會依其本國法律決定是否給予保護。

台灣並非馬德里體系的成員。因此，以台灣為基地的申請人無法以台灣的申請案作為馬德里國際申請的基礎。實務上，針對東協市場的商標必須向各市場的國家智慧財產局逐國申請，或透過各司法管轄區的當地代理人或律師辦理。

馬德里體系不會產生全球性的商標，也不處理專利登記。對許多申請人而言，直接向各國提出申請本來就是標準途徑；即使是符合馬德里體系資格的申請人，直接申請也可能是合適的選擇。

請依據品牌、商品或服務，以及涉及的司法管轄區，選擇合適的申請途徑。

## WIPO 與東協的調解機制

若發生爭議，WIPO-ASEAN Mediation Programme（WIPO 與東協調解計畫，簡稱 AMP+）為符合條件的智慧財產權與科技相關案件提供調解框架。

該計畫在符合其條件的情況下提供經費補助。請向 WIPO 確認目前的資格要件與受理情況。[WIPO：東協調解計畫](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/office-singapore/wipo-asean-mediation-programme)

調解需要雙方同意參與，且不保證達成和解。應結合爭議的具體情況，以及相關司法管轄區可採取的執行手段，一併評估。

本指南提及的機構為 WIPO，負責馬德里體系的管理及其調解服務。當地的登記事務則由各東協市場的國家智慧財產局辦理。
